subproblem.title: Almost every slice defect has finite mass on bounded sets
subproblem.statement: Assume (MM), the third conjunct of the frozen statement of the sibling cbr_measure_convergence_tools: for every P ∈ ℕ, all measures μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) on ℝ^P, every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, every G ⊆ ℝ^P, all a, b ∈ ℝ, every L ∈ ℝ≥0 and all Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] (j ∈ ℕ) with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for every j and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹·μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every j and every t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_{j→∞} Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dt ≤ L·liminf_{j→∞} μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Let P, q ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, Z : ℝ → 𝒟_q(U) (t ↦ Z_t), a measure μ on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, a continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ and L ∈ ℝ≥0, and assume M_W(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P and every t ∈ ℝ. Here M_W(T) := T.massOn W, h⁻¹ is read as ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹, and the liminf is taken along 𝓝[>] 0 in [0, ∞]. Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ one has M_W(Z_t) < ∞ for every bounded W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ j, μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}) < ∞) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (t : ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → Z j t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs j (G ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => Z j t) atTop ≤ g t) ∧ ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun j => μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})) atTop) → ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Z : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U q) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), Continuous f → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (t : ℝ), IsOpen W → (Z t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (W ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), Bornology.IsBounded W → (Z t).massOn W < ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cbr_cc_slice_property_of_im, isolated for an arbitrary family Z of currents with the liminf mass bound. The parent applies it with U := ℝ^P, q := d, Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t and the bound supplied by (SL); f is continuous because it is Lipschitz.
Notation: M_W(T) := T.massOn W; B_k := ball(0, k) (open) and B̄_k := closedBall(0, k) for k ∈ ℕ; volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
1. (Setup.) Fix k, m ∈ ℕ and put G := B_k, a := −m, b := m. Since G ∩ {a < f < b} ⊆ B_k ⊆ B̄_k and B̄_k is compact (isCompact_closedBall; ℝ^P is proper), μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}) ≤ μ(B̄_k) < ∞ (measure_mono and the hypothesis on μ).
2. (Applying (MM).) Apply (MM) with P, the constant sequence μ_j := μ (j ∈ ℕ), f, G, a, b, L and the constant sequence Z_j(t) := M_{B_k}(Z_t) (j ∈ ℕ, t ∈ ℝ). Its hypotheses hold: f is continuous; μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for every j by step 1; and for every j and every t ∈ (a, b), Z_j(t) = M_{B_k}(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹·μ(B_k ∩ {t − h < f < t}) by the hypothesis on Z applied to the open set W := B_k (isOpen_ball). (MM) yields a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with (i) liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t such that t ∈ (a, b), and (ii) ∫_{(a,b)} g dt ≤ L·liminf_j μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}).
3. (Constant sequences.) The filter atTop on ℕ is nontrivial, so the liminf of a constant sequence equals its value (Filter.liminf_const). Thus (i) says: for a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies M_{B_k}(Z_t) ≤ g(t); and (ii) says ∫_{(−m,m)} g dt ≤ L·μ(B_k ∩ {−m < f < m}), which is < ∞ because (L : [0, ∞]) < ∞ and by step 1 (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
4. (Finiteness of g.) g is measurable and its integral with respect to volume⌞(−m, m) is finite, so g(t) < ∞ for volume⌞(−m, m)-a.e. t (ae_lt_top). Since (−m, m) is measurable, this means: for a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies g(t) < ∞ (ae_restrict_iff'). Intersecting with step 3: for a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies M_{B_k}(Z_t) ≤ g(t) < ∞.
5. (Countable intersection.) ℕ is countable, so by ae_all_iff, applied over k and then over m, there is one Lebesgue-null set N such that for every t ∉ N and all k, m ∈ ℕ: t ∈ (−m, m) implies M_{B_k}(Z_t) < ∞.
6. (Conclusion.) Let t ∉ N and let W ⊆ ℝ^P be bounded. Then W ⊆ ball(0, r) for some r ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball). Choose k ∈ ℕ with r < k (exists_nat_gt), so W ⊆ B_k (ball_subset_ball). Choose m ∈ ℕ with |t| < m, so −m < t < m. By monotonicity of the local mass in the region (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono) and step 5, M_W(Z_t) ≤ M_{B_k}(Z_t) < ∞. Since N is null, for L¹-a.e. t this holds for every bounded W. ∎
Appendix (verified Lean). This tactic proof of exactly the frozen statement compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission inside namespace GMT.Ch07 with the contract's opens. #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
  intro hMM P q U Z μ f L hf hμ hZ
  have key : ∀ k m : ℕ, ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo (-(m : ℝ)) m →
      (Z t).massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) k) < ∞ := by
    intro k m
    have hfinG : μ (ball (0 : Euclid P) k ∩ {x | -(m : ℝ) < f x ∧ f x < m}) < ∞ :=
      (measure_mono (inter_subset_left.trans ball_subset_closedBall)).trans_lt
        (hμ _ (isCompact_closedBall _ _))
    obtain ⟨g, hg, hle, hint⟩ := hMM P (fun _ => μ) f (ball (0 : Euclid P) k) (-(m : ℝ)) m L
      (fun _ t => (Z t).massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) k)) hf (fun _ => hfinG)
      (fun _ t _ => hZ _ t isOpen_ball)
    simp only [liminf_const] at hle hint
    have hint' : ∫⁻ t in Ioo (-(m : ℝ)) m, g t ≠ ∞ :=
      (hint.trans_lt (ENNReal.mul_lt_top ENNReal.coe_lt_top hfinG)).ne
    have hgfin : ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Ioo (-(m : ℝ)) m)), g t < ∞ := ae_lt_top hg hint'
    rw [ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Ioo] at hgfin
    filter_upwards [hle, hgfin] with t h1 h2 ht
    exact (h1 ht).trans_lt (h2 ht)
  have key2 : ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ k m : ℕ, t ∈ Ioo (-(m : ℝ)) m →
      (Z t).massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) k) < ∞ := by
    rw [ae_all_iff]; intro k; rw [ae_all_iff]; exact key k
  filter_upwards [key2] with t ht W hW
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := hW.subset_ball (0 : Euclid P)
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_nat_gt r
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := exists_nat_gt |t|
  have htm : t ∈ Ioo (-(m : ℝ)) m := ⟨by linarith [neg_abs_le t], by linarith [le_abs_self t]⟩
  exact ((Z t).massOn_mono (hr.trans (ball_subset_ball hk.le))).trans_lt (ht k m htm)
proof_key_steps: For k, m ∈ ℕ, apply (MM) on (−m, m) to the constant sequences μ_j := μ and Z_j(t) := M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t), with G := B_k(0); here μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ μ(B̄_k(0)) < ∞.
Since the sequences are constant, M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) ≤ g(t) a.e. on (−m, m) and ∫_{(−m,m)} g < ∞; so g, and hence M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t), is finite a.e. on (−m, m) (ae_lt_top, ae_restrict_iff').
Intersect over the countably many k, m (ae_all_iff). Every bounded W lies in some B_k(0) and every t in some (−m, m), so M_W(Z_t) ≤ M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ (massOn_mono).

subproblem.title: Borel restrictions of admissible representations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Assume (IMC)(b): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R in U of degree n and every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with R'.Represents A, R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient. Assume (IMC)(d): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P and every IMRep R in U of degree n, for Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. x (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) one has |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. Assume (RU), the frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq: for all P, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, all measures μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ on ℝ^P that are finite on every compact subset of U and all fields ξ₁, ξ₂, ξ₃ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) such that each ξ_i is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable and satisfies |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ_i-a.e. x and every k-covector α, if ∫ ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫ ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫ ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), then ∫_B ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫_B ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫_B ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃ for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P and every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Let P, q ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let X, A ∈ 𝒟_q(U) with X integer multiplicity. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_q(ℝ^P) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and every q-covector α, such that X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U). Let E ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set with A(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U) (Bochner integrals). Then A is integer multiplicity.

Source: steps 3–5 of the supplied proof of cbr_cc_slice_property_of_im (the proofs that A_t and B_t are integer multiplicity), isolated for an arbitrary integer multiplicity X ∈ 𝒟_q(U), an arbitrary admissible representation (μ, ξ) of X and an arbitrary Borel set E. The parent applies it twice with U := ℝ^P and E := {f < t}: with (q, X, μ, ξ, A) := (d + 1, X, μ, ξ, A_t) and with (q, X, μ, ξ, A) := (d, ∂X, μ', ξ', B_t). Step 3 of the supplied proof is provided by the reused siblings imrep_data (cmc_fcl_imrep_integral_data) and imrep_restrict (cmc_fcl_imrep_restrict_formula).
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for a field ζ and a form ω, ζ(ω) denotes the function x ↦ ζ(x)(ω(x)); H^q := μHE[q].
1. (Representation of X.) Since X is integer multiplicity, there is an IMRep R_X = (M, θ, ζ) in U of degree q with R_X.Represents X. Put ν := R_X.measure = (H^q⌞M).withDensity θ.
2. (Restricted IMRep.) U is open and E is Borel, so (IMC)(b) applied to R_X and E gives a current A' ∈ 𝒟_q(U) and an IMRep R' in U with R'.Represents A', R'.carrier = M ∩ E, R'.mult = θ and R'.orient = ζ.
3. (Admissibility of (ν, ζ).) The sibling imrep_data applied to the current X and its representation R_X gives: (a) ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (b) ζ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) if |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α for H^q⌞M-a.e. x, then the same holds for ν-a.e. x; (d) X(ω) = ∫ ζ(ω) dν for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U). The hypothesis of (c) is exactly (IMC)(d) for R_X, so |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α holds for ν-a.e. x.
4. (Applying (RU).) Apply (RU) with k := q, the open set U, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ, ξ), (μ₂, ξ₂) := (ν, ζ) and (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0), the zero measure with the zero field x ↦ 0. Its hypotheses hold. Finiteness on compact subsets of U: for μ by assumption, for ν by 3(a), and trivially for the zero measure. A.e. strong measurability: for ξ by assumption, for ζ by 3(b), and for the constant field 0 because constant functions are strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_const). Unit bounds: for ξ by assumption, for ζ by step 3, and for the zero measure because every property holds a.e. for it (its a.e. filter is ⊥). The identity: for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U), ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = X(ω) = ∫ ζ(ω) dν = ∫ ζ(ω) dν + ∫ 0 d0, by the representation hypothesis on (μ, ξ), by 3(d), and because every integral against the zero measure is 0 (integral_zero_measure). The conclusion of (RU) with the Borel set B := E gives, for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U), ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν + ∫_E 0 d0 = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν, because the restriction of the zero measure is the zero measure (Measure.restrict_zero) and its integral vanishes.
5. (Applying imrep_restrict.) The sibling imrep_restrict applied to R := R_X, R', A' and E (E Borel, R' represents A', carrier(R') = M ∩ E, mult(R') = θ, orient(R') = ζ) gives A'(ω) = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U).
6. (Conclusion.) For every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U), A(ω) = ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ (hypothesis on A) = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν (step 4) = A'(ω) (step 5) = R'.action(ω) (R' represents A'). Hence R'.Represents A, so A is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity A is witnessed by R'). ∎
